qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: On-campus medical office buildings possess localized tenant stickiness and health system integration, and senior housing clusters have local operating presence. However, empirical proof of moat fails decisively: 15-year GAAP ROIC has structurally fluctuated between 1.1% and 3.0% (far below the 12% threshold). Capital intensity, high recurring property maintenance capex, operator dependence, and local supply competition prevent economic rent extraction.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Proof of Moat, REJECT). Ventas is a major healthcare REIT with senior housing operating portfolio (SHOP), outpatient medical buildings, and life science properties. While demographic aging provides volume demand, the business model is highly capital-intensive and subject to operator risk and local market oversupply. 15-year historical GAAP ROIC has structurally ranged between 1.1% and 3.0%, falling far short of the 12% Munger moat threshold. This is a structural feature of capital-intensive real estate, not a temporary fixable calamity.
qualitative.evidence: 15-year historical ROIC peaked at ~3.0% in 2016-2018 and compressed to 1.10%-1.82% in 2021-2024 (2.16% in 2025), consistently and dramatically below the 12% ROIC requirement for Gate 3b. Real estate assets require heavy ongoing capex and debt financing (Net Debt/EBITDA ~5.2x-6.0x, interest coverage ~1.0x-1.3x in 2024-2025). The asset class structurally lacks excess economic return compounding.
